title: Free-seeder-flora foundational growth architecture
scope: Foundational strategy of the K3 free-seeder kingdom at qualitative grain; usable within shared-setting ecology and adopted downstream story development.
claims: Free-seeders are individual, non-networked, short-lived, fast-growing plants.
They specialise in openings: disturbed ground, fire scars, flood scours, trample gaps, and abandoned worked land.
They are poor long-term competitors against established stands and persist by exploiting change rather than holding ground.
The kingdom's signature is the seed vault: a durable dormant capsule that can wait in soil for years or decades until disturbance cues wake it.
The population's persistent form is the buried vault bank; growing plants are cheap, fast, and brief.
Disturbed ground erupts primarily from vault banks already present, and old worked or cleared land can carry buried seed legacies.
Dispersal exists but is secondary at kingdom grain.
boundaries: Free-seeder, seed vault, and vault bank are author-facing functional descriptions, not in-world names or formal taxonomy.
The strategy establishes no Earth annual, weed, seed-bank, or other plant homology.
Species, forms, sizes, silhouettes, chemistry, energy capture, and growth habits remain open.

Vault anatomy, dormancy limits, longevity, cue specifics, viability decay, bank densities, and depth behaviour remain open; no vault is guaranteed viable, and banks can be exhausted, destroyed, or absent.
Buried legacies are a possibility of old worked land, not a guarantee at any particular place; no specific clearance, field, or site is established as carrying one.
Eruption from existing banks is the primary pattern, not an exclusive rule; arrival by dispersal remains possible and its mechanisms remain open.
Crop-ancestor potential is niche-space description only; no crop, domestication, cultivation, weed status, or human practice is established.
No free-seeder member is established as present, dominant, or absent at any particular location.
Interactions with K1 openings dynamics remain governed by the reserve-web records where they overlap; this record adds no reserve-web claim.
Grazing, pests, diseases, symbioses including any K6 partnership, and animal dispersal relationships remain open.
Earth and mythological inspiration remains author-facing; no living, extinct, or legendary Earth species is transplanted.

Mana patterns remain open; no Mana organ, specialised ability, System progression, spawn point, refill node, guaranteed harvest, reward, Skill, trait payload, or Ancestry Development rule is established.
Water, energy, nutrients, space, growth time, disturbance, disease, and decay remain binding ecological constraints.
story_implications: Scenes can show plough-woken flushes, fire-following blooms, and abandoned clearances erupting with growth.
Old worked land can carry buried seed legacies from before the collapse, discovered only when disturbed.
Fields gain grounded weed pressure from their own buried banks.
Every species, site, legacy, and event requires its own evidence and records.
system_implications: The strategy describes ordinary planetary ecology under CAL0 WLD1.2D and WLD2.1A+D.
No System mechanic, germination guarantee, spawn source, refill node, reward, or specialised Mana ability is established.
research_questions: What vault anatomy, chemistry, and dormancy mechanisms implement the strategy?
What cue combinations wake vaults, and how do banks decay?
Which members are candidate crop ancestors or persistent field weeds?
What dispersal mechanisms move vaults between openings?
Which animal, pest, and K6 relationships shape vault survival?
How do vault banks interact with reserve-web openings and recovery?

author_approval.evidence: After the A/B/C strategy cards were presented with A recommended, the Author selected 'A — Vault-seed' on 2026-08-17.
